summary: Samuel Swinton Jacob was an engineer active in the field of history and archaeology. He was educated at Cheam School and studied at the Addiscombe Military Seminary from around 1856 to 1858.
Samuel Tickell worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Addiscombe Military Seminary from 1827 to 1829 and served in the Bengal Army from circa 1829 to 1865.
Samuel Wells Williams worked in sinology and linguistics. He studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute from around 1831 to 1832 and held a post at Yale University from circa 1877 to 1884.

Samuel William Fallon worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned a Ph.D. from Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg by 1862 and served as an inspector of schools for the Bengal Education Department from circa 1854 to 1878.

Sandamali Udeshika Dissanayaka works in Buddhist studies. She earned a BA from the University of Sri Jayewardenepura (2017–2021) and an MA from the University of Kelaniya (2023–2024), becoming a Temporary Lecturer at the University of Ruhuna in 2024.

Sandeep Namdev Dhikale works in Indology and religious studies, holding an M.A. from Savitribai Phule Pune University. His posts include positions at Fergusson College, the Ministry of Education, MIT World Peace University (2019–2020), and SARTHI (2020–2022).
Sandford Arnot was an Indology and linguistics scholar. In 1826, he succeeded John Borthwick Gilchrist and served as a teacher of Hindustani at the Oriental Institution, Leicester Square.

Sandford Arthur Strong worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at King's College London, under Cecil Bendall, at St John's College, and Oxford. He taught Arabic at UCL (1895) and Assyriology at Cambridge (c. 1895–1903).

Sandra A. Wawrytko is a scholar in philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies. She held posts at San Diego State University, attested as Professor in 1999 and Associate Professor of Philosophy in 2014, and taught Michael J. Tetreault.
Sandra Bell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Durham University by 1991 and served as a professor there in 1991.

Sandra Hochwarter is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Vienna, earning a Mag.phil. under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes, with Anne MacDonald as her teacher.
Sang-Kyun Sun works in Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Delhi under supervisor Sanghasen Singh and served as a lecturer at JinGak Buddhist College, both attested in 1995.

Sanga Tenzin specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a BSc from Navodaya Education Trust (2012–2016), worked at Central Regional Referral Hospital (2018), and is attested in 2026 at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Sangay Dorji is a Tibetology and linguistics scholar who studied at Tengtho Monastery and Semtokha Rigney School, where he later taught. He served as Secretary of the Dzongkha Development Commission (attested 1999–2004) and Specialist at the Ministry of Education (2022).

Sangeeta Abhay Patil works in Indology. She studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University, earning an MD between 2005 and 2007, and served as an Academic Consultant at Yashwantrao Chavan Maharashtra Open University in 2023.

Sangharakshita was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who founded the Triratna Buddhist Community in 1967. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and under teachers including Jagdish Kashyap, Chien Ming Chen, Dhardo Rinpoche, and Dudjom Rinpoche.

Sangseraima Ujeed is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed a doctorate at the University of Oxford (circa 2012–2018) and held a postdoctoral fellowship at the University of California, Santa Barbara from circa 2018 to 2020.

Sangye Tenzin was a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who served as Abbot of Menri Monastery and taught Yongdzin Tenzin Namdak and Matthew T. Kapstein. He is attested in 2026 as a doctoral student at Virginia.

Sangyeob Cha is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned a Ph.D. from Dongguk University (2001–2008), worked as an HK Professor at Geumgang University (2011–2022), and was a researcher at Kyungpook National University (2020).

Sanit Sinak works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He earned degrees from Mahamakut Buddhist University, Ramkhamhaeng University, and Silpakorn University, and served as an instructor at Mahamakut Buddhist University in 2014.
